center.title: Media Purge
center.subtitle: Reclaim storage by removing MEDIA you no longer need — policy-driven, explainable and reversible. (To delete junk files left by a download, use Junk file removal in Media Settings instead.)
center.howItWorks: Media Purge proposes; people decide. A run turns policy matches into candidates — nothing is removed. A candidate becomes an action only inside an approved plan whose fingerprints still match the world, and every removal lands in Trash or Quarantine, both recoverable.

tile.policiesDesc: Versioned purge policies and their conditions
tile.runsDesc: Scans and the candidates they produced
tile.plansDesc: Review and approve what a run proposed
tile.protectionsDesc: What an automatic purge may never touch

policies.title: Purge Policies
policies.subtitle: A policy is a draft plus frozen published versions. Publishing does not enable it — arming a destructive policy is a separate, deliberate act.
policies.emptyDesc: Start from a template or create an empty policy, then publish and enable it when you are ready.

draft.title: Policy document (draft)
draft.help: The policy is a JSON document evaluated by the platform's constrained engine — there is no code and nothing executable. A full visual condition builder is planned; for now, edit the document directly.

policies.confirmDelete: Delete this policy and all its versions? This cannot be undone.
policies.confirmEnable: Enable this policy? An enabled, published policy can be run by a schedule or trigger.
policies.publishFirst: Publish the policy before running it.

runs.title: Purge Runs
runs.subtitle: A run walks a policy's scope and records what it found. It produces candidates, never deletions.
runs.emptyDesc: Run or simulate a policy to see candidates here.

plans.title: Plans & Approvals
plans.subtitle: A plan pins the policy version and each candidate's fingerprint, so what you approve is exactly what runs. Approval grants permission to act; execution acts, re-checking everything first.
plans.emptyDesc: Build a plan from a run's candidates to see it here.
plans.confirmApprove: Approve this plan? It grants permission to remove the listed files to {{destination}}.
plans.confirmExecute: Execute this plan now? Each file is re-checked immediately before it is touched; anything protected, locked, busy or changed is skipped.
plans.rejectReason: Why are you rejecting this plan?

quarantine.title: Quarantine
quarantine.subtitle: Held files, moved out of the library but never deleted. Restore puts a file back exactly where it came from; purge is the one irreversible step.
quarantine.emptyDesc: Media a purge plan quarantined will appear here until restored or purged.
quarantine.confirmRestore: Restore this file to its original location?
quarantine.confirmPurge: Permanently delete this file? This bypasses Trash and cannot be undone.
quarantine.overwrite: Overwrite whatever is now at the original path

protections.title: Protections
protections.subtitle: A protection tells an automatic purge it may never touch something. Conditional protections fail closed; a legal hold cannot be lifted by an ordinary operator.
protections.emptyDesc: Protect a file, library, show, tag or path so a purge can never remove it.
protections.confirmRevoke: Revoke this protection? A purge will be free to act on the target again.
protections.revokeReason: Why are you revoking this protection?

create.title: New protection
create.reasonPlaceholder: Why this exists — required for the audit trail

oldUnwatchedLowRes.name: Old, unwatched, low-resolution movies
oldUnwatchedLowRes.desc: Movies released before 2001, never watched, below 1080p.
oldUnwatchedLowRes.rationale: Old low-res films nobody has played are the safest first thing to reclaim. Approval required.

lowUse10bit.name: Low-use 10-bit media
lowUse10bit.rationale: Report only — 10-bit is usually the better encode, so this flags for review rather than removal.

supersededH264.name: Superseded 8-bit H.264 with a verified replacement
supersededH264.desc: 8-bit H.264 files where an equal-or-better copy already exists.
supersededH264.rationale: Quarantine, approval required — only ever with a verified surviving replacement.

cond.mediaKind.desc: Movie, TV episode, anime and so on. Use this to keep a policy off a kind you never want touched.
cond.releaseYear.desc: The year the title was released — not when you added it. For 'old films', this is the one you want.
cond.releaseDate.desc: Full release date, when a year is too coarse.
cond.genre.desc: Matches if any of the title's genres contains your text.
cond.certification.desc: Certification such as PG-13 or TV-MA, when the provider supplied one.
cond.runtime.desc: Length from the metadata provider. For the measured length of your file, use Duration instead.
cond.rating.desc: Provider rating out of 10. Absent for anything unidentified.
cond.matchStatus.desc: Whether the item was identified automatically, by hand, or not at all.
cond.hasExternalId.desc: True when the item is linked to TMDB/IMDb. Unlinked items are usually unidentified.
cond.metadataComplete.desc: True when the core fields were filled in by a provider.
cond.inCollection.desc: Part of a collection you have assembled.
cond.onWatchlist.desc: Something you marked to watch — a strong reason NOT to delete it.
cond.tag.desc: Matches if any of the item's tags contains your text.
cond.neverWatched.desc: Nobody has ever completed a play. Depends on your media server reporting history.
cond.completedPlays.desc: How many times it was watched to the end, across all users.
cond.startedPlays.desc: How many times playback began, finished or not.
cond.uniqueViewers.desc: How many different people have played it.
cond.lastPlayedAt.desc: When it was last played by anyone.
cond.daysSinceLastPlay.desc: Easier than a date for 'not touched in a year' rules.
cond.maxProgress.desc: The furthest anyone got. Someone 80% through has not abandoned it.
cond.watchedByNoUsers.desc: No user has any play history for it.
cond.watchedByAllUsers.desc: Every user has watched it — often a keeper.
cond.traktWatched.desc: Marked watched in Trakt, even if this server never played it.
cond.resolutionClass.desc: 480p, 720p, 1080p, 2160p — compared in order, so 'below 1080p' works as you would expect.
cond.width.desc: Exact frame width, when resolution class is too coarse.
cond.videoCodec.desc: x264, x265/HEVC, AV1 and so on.
cond.videoBitDepth.desc: 8-bit or 10-bit. 10-bit files are larger and not all devices play them.
cond.audioCodec.desc: AAC, AC3, DTS, TrueHD and so on.
cond.bitrate.desc: Overall bitrate. A rough proxy for quality within one codec, misleading across codecs.
cond.duration.desc: Measured length of your file — the honest one. Differs from Runtime when a file is trimmed or mis-identified.
cond.techSource.desc: Whether these values were measured by a probe or guessed from the filename.
cond.probeFailed.desc: The file could not be measured. Treat its technical values with suspicion.
cond.fileSize.desc: Size on disk of the media file.
cond.fileAgeDays.desc: How long the file has existed on disk.
cond.addedAt.desc: When this item first appeared in your library.
cond.addedAgeDays.desc: How long you have had it. Useful for 'give anything new a grace period'.
cond.totalTitleSize.desc: All files for the title together — the whole season rather than one episode.
cond.libraryFreePercent.desc: Free space on the drive holding the library, at evaluation time.
cond.isDuplicate.desc: The Duplicate Center considers this one of several copies.
cond.betterReplacement.desc: Another copy of the same title scores higher on quality.
cond.torrentActive.desc: Still managed by a torrent client — removing the file may break seeding.
cond.torrentRatio.desc: Upload/download ratio, when the torrent is still tracked.
cond.libraryKind.desc: Movies, TV, music and so on.
cond.pathPrefix.desc: Restrict to a folder. Use it to fence a policy into one area of the disk.
cond.isLocked.desc: Locked items are excluded from automation regardless of any policy.
cond.isProtected.desc: Matched by a protection rule in Media Purge.
cond.hasActiveJob.desc: Something is operating on it right now.
cond.activePlayback.desc: Someone is watching it at this moment.
cond.ambiguousIdentity.desc: The item's identification is uncertain — deleting on uncertain identity is how the wrong film gets removed.
cond.pendingDuplicate.desc: It sits in an unresolved duplicate group.

builder.noConditions: No conditions yet — a policy with none would match your entire library, so nothing will run until you add at least one.
builder.elevated: Depends on playback history. If your media server has not reported watches, this may be true for things you have actually watched.
builder.measured: Needs a measured file. Items that were never probed are skipped rather than guessed at.
builder.preserved: This policy also contains advanced settings the builder does not edit (replacement rules, storage-pressure triggers or nested condition groups). They are kept exactly as they are.

mode.approval_required: Ask me to approve each item

modeHelp.report_only: Builds a list and stops. Nothing is moved or deleted. Start here — run it, read the list, and only then decide whether the conditions are right.
modeHelp.approval_required: Builds a list and waits for you. Nothing moves until you approve it item by item.
modeHelp.auto_quarantine: Moves matching items to quarantine on its own, with no approval. They are recoverable until the retention period ends.
modeHelp.auto_trash: Deletes matching items on its own, with no approval. Only choose this once a report-only run has shown you exactly what it selects.
